name: Tandanya National Aboriginal Cultural Institute
watch: Australia's oldest Aboriginal-owned and governed multi-arts cultural centre, operating on Kaurna Yarta since 1989.

name: Tashkeel
funding: Founded 2008, paid for privately by founder Sheikha Lateefa bint Maktoum plus project partners such as Van Cleef & Arpels (luxury) and Dubai Culture
watch: Non-profit studio, residency and gallery that also runs a commercial consultancy. ENOC, Dubai's state oil company, commissioned work through it for Expo 2020.
records_note: No annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; the about page names founder Sheikha Lateefa bint Maktoum and the team page lists staff only.

name: TAVROS
watch: Mid-sized non-profit space in the post-industrial Tavros neighborhood exploring civic responsibility and local community.

name: TAXISPALAIS Kunsthalle Tirol
funding: Tirol's regional kunsthalle; funders not named in readable site text.
records_note: Its parent Tiroler Landesmuseen posts 2024 and 2025 reports, a balance sheet in the Land Tirol holdings report and its supervisory board; funders are logos.

name: Tbilisi Photography & Multimedia Museum (TPMM)
funding: Small NGO museum (founded 2017) in Stamba Hotel; funded by Swiss SDC, Adjara Group/Stamba, Prince Claus Fund, OSGF, MG Law, MagiC Carpets.
watch: Moved some operations to a Lithuanian NGO after Georgia's 2024 foreign-agent law.
records_note: No annual reports or accounts found; a Donors and Partners footer block shows seven named-in-alt logos with no date, and no board is listed.

name: Te Papa
funding: NZ$85M revenue (2024-25), Crown 52%. Its current partners page lists Panasonic, Bloomberg, Samsung, MyLotto and gaming-machine trusts PubCharity and Lion Foundation.
watch: Both raise money from gaming machines. Named Te Taiao | Nature grant partners at its 2019 opening and again in the 2024-25 annual report.
records_note: It posts annual reports from 2000-01 to 2024-25 with Auditor-General accounts, names its eight board members and lists partners without a date.

name: Te Uru Waitakere Contemporary Gallery
funding: Core funding from the Waitākere Ranges Local Board (Auckland Council). It also takes gifts from a Benefactors Collective and sponsors, none named.
watch: Income was NZ$1.17M in the year to June 2024.
records_note: No annual reports on its site; the NZ register holds returns to June 2024. One council funder is named; the About page lists the board.

name: Teatro Real
funding: Ministry of Culture, Comunidad de Madrid, ticket subscriptions, and corporate sponsor board.

name: TEOR/éTica
funding: Private non-profit founded 1999 by Virginia Pérez-Ratton; funders not disclosed.
records_note: Shows three undated funder logos in its footer and lists staff, but publishes no annual reports, accounts or board.

name: Thailand Biennale
funding: 2025-26 edition: Ministry of Culture's Office of Contemporary Art and Culture with Phuket province; commissions co-funded by unnamed foundations.
watch: State-run; commissions are co-funded by unnamed foundations.
records_note: Could not check: the biennale site returned 403 and 429 blocks, so nothing was confirmed beyond its government organisers.

name: The Common Guild
funding: £379k income (FY2025). Creative Scotland plus grants from Ampersand, Henry Moore, Elephant Trust, Pro Helvetia, British Council Scotland, Goethe-Institut, Culture Ireland, Hope Scott Trust and individuals.
watch: Its thanks list names Outset; a November 2024 open letter asked Tate to divest from it. No current Outset credit found.
records_note: No annual reports, only a diversity report; OSCR holds accounts 2021 to 2025; the support page names funders undated; the board is listed.
